To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of the plant growth regulator, azetidine-2-carboxyic acid (AZC), to barley seedlings, results in a decrease in root hydraulic conductivity (L p), which is not accompanied by a decrease in root water permeability (L p/w).
azetidine-2-carboxyic acid (AZC), a structural analogue of proline, inhibits the uptake of water by barley roots, but does not inhibit the uptake of proline.

the inhibition of ion release to the root xylem by the amino acid analog azetidine 3-carboxylic (AzC) acid does not result in a reduction in root hydraulic conductivity (L p), and that the L p of roots is not affected by the application of AzC acid to the root surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the amino acid analogue azetidine  2‐carboylc acid (ACA) on the transport of ions in barley roots.
the effects of the amino acid analogue azetidine-2-carboxyic acid (AzA) on the transport of ions and water in the barley root.
the effects of a number of compounds on the hydraulic conductivity of barley root systems, with the object of obtaining information on the mechanism of action of the compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the azetidine carboxylic acids are not only inhibitors of the aminoacyl tRNA synthetase, as was previously shown, but also inhibitors of the elongation factor Tu, and that this inhibition is due to a competition for the same binding site on EF‐Tu.
azetidine 3-carboxylic acids are potent inhibitors of root growth and of ion transport in barley.
A2C inhibits the transport of ions to the xylems of roots, and that this inhibition is due to a reduction in the rate of ion uptake by the root.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the azetidine 3-carboxylic and the 2-azetidone carboxylic acids are potent and specific inhibitors of the transport of ions across the root to xylem.
azetidine 3-carboxylic (ACA) acid inhibits ion movement from barley roots by inhibiting a carrier‐mediated process.
the inhibition of root growth by azetidine carboxylic acid (ACA) is due to inhibition of ion uptake and transport, not to inhibition of water transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the root system of the plants is a key component of the plant’s water uptake.
the inhibition of root ion release by azetidine-2-carboxyic acid is not accompanied by a reduction in root hydraulic conductance.

the inhibition of root growth is not a direct effect of azetidine‐2‐carboxylate on the root cell wall, and that the inhibition of ion movement across the cell wall is not the primary cause of inhibition of root elongation.
